changes.evidence: Two separate short horizontal ink strokes stand above the text at the right; they do not form a visible numeral.

The cancellation crosses the last letter bodies. The initial c, t ascender, accent, and g descender are visible, but the terminal e/s sequence cannot be separated reliably. The deletion itself is definite.

changes.location: Opening replacement above the cancelled noun
changes.evidence: The word champs, including a separate terminal s, is written above the cancelled noun rather than on its baseline.
The g descender and following tall l are clear. Raised accent-like points are visible, but the compressed final low strokes do not decide whether one or two e bodies precede s.
The mark after M is a small isolated point without a descending hook. The following mark after N has a conspicuous hooked comma, providing a local shape comparison.

A small dark hooked mark sits to the right of the raised en, above the separate accent/dot belonging to the baseline à. Its comma-like form is visible, but whether it is intentional punctuation remains uncertain.
The gap after the terminal d and before the looped l contains no comma stroke; the end of d belongs to the letter.

changes.location: Cancelled capital immediately before L tensor L
changes.evidence: Two surviving upright portions and intersecting diagonals favor N, while the lower rightward stroke still allows L. The dense cancellation prevents a certain recovery. This is a mathematical glyph, so the partial reading is retained with alternatives.

The dotted initial i, t cross-stroke, p descender, later tall t, and final e are visible. The compressed medial letters and the first of the two final e bodies remain insufficiently distinct for an unqualified reading.
The last short vowel is a low e-shaped body feeding the looped l, without the extra upright return of a. The preceding u-n-i-v-e-r-s sequence is also visible.
Two high strokes at each end form the quotation marks. There are no angular guillemet chevrons.

changes.location: Cancelled short word after splittée colon
changes.evidence: The surviving short rising strokes and low tail favor un, but a cancelled l/a ligature cannot be excluded. No intact tall loop decides the first letter. The crossed-out state is definite; only the letters are doubtful.
Two adjacent tall t stems with joined cross-strokes are followed directly by a small final e. No ou is present.
The two i dots are distinct from the short grave stroke above è; the final m/e run is joined but complete. This crop confirms the agreed reading.
A low u-shaped beginning and following n upstroke form un. The apparent extra density is the connecting stroke, not another word or a deletion.

The first r and e are followed by low medial strokes and a late tall t with a terminal e. There is no tall l in the position required by relève. The flattened o/n portion still warrants doubt in remonte.

The beginning of termes is a live tall t and attached e, followed by the joined rmes. No separate crossed-out cluster precedes it. Half b also shows no extra cancelled word at the end of the preceding line.
Paired high opening and closing strokes surround the word; neither side has a guillemet angle.

notes: Author claim: the invariant sigma is obtained from the symmetry of L tensor L, interpreted as a section of left-indexed 2N. The phrase s'obtient en and L are visibly interlinear insertions.

Author claim with explicit qualification: Je sais prouver (sauf erreur) asserts that every homomorphism M → ₂N comes from a suitable Picard champ. The author locates an obstruction in Ext³(X;M,N) and says an argument quoted as universel proves it vanishes.
Author claim: the extension (*) is close to split because sections lift; the text calls the resulting section ensembliste. A stronger claim refers to a class in a degree-2 hypercohomology group on U.

The final formula's script/calligraphic H, E versus underlined F, low point between M and N, and small mark after N were read from the ink. Expected notation or balanced parentheses was not used to normalize them.
The author's explicit doubt wording is sauf erreur. Other unsure marks in this reading record transcription uncertainty, not additional author qualifications.
No author page number is visibly legible. H's page{5} is treated as its editorial page label, not imported as manuscript ink. The archive pencil foliation reads 63 and is a TeX comment.

The top-right strokes are independent marginal marks. The left and bottom boundaries and the heavy lower-right vertical mark are reproduction features, recorded in a comment, not counted as omitted words or author drawings.

No mathematical proof, counterexample, derivation, or use-as-background check was performed. The checks list is therefore empty. Inspecting exponents, indices, separators, and bracket strokes is transcription work, not a proof check.

coverage: The whole source image was viewed once for layout and dimensions, then supplied half a and half b were each viewed once sequentially. Every prose line was compared against the complete C and H witnesses, including agreed words, accents, endings, punctuation, inline mathematical signs, arrow direction, left indices, exponents, quotations, insertion guides, and deletion states. Fourteen tight crops were created only for loci unresolved by the halves and were each viewed once; every crop was made with crop.py and is logged. The page contains one continuous handwritten paragraph with inline formulas, three interlinear replacements/additions, two cancelled word/capital loci beyond the opening cancelled noun, two upper-right strokes, and archive foliation; there are no displayed equations, author drawings, or diagrams. H expands tte, uses a different lifting verb and H alphabet, gives an extra deletion before termes and an extra i.e. at the end, and does not represent the upper-right strokes or archive foliation in the supplied page text. A possible low point in the final argument list is recorded with uncertainty instead of silently omitted. Retained C doubts and the additional punctuation doubt are listed explicitly, with original whole-page source boxes. No other pages, other readers, OCR, external text, or research were consulted.
